## Mathematical increment

Let C_j be a known depth-5 failed germ set (R303 hereditary theorem), j from 0 to m-1, and let I_g={j:g in C_j}. For a queried branch A, the exact index of failed cores contained in A is

J(A)=[0,m) minus union over g not in A of I_g.

Proof: j belongs to J(A) iff no germ of C_j lies outside A, iff C_j is a subset of A. Thus nonempty J(A) is a sound hereditary rejection by R303. The representation uses one m-bit incidence vector per germ, intersects complements for every absent germ, and stops only when the intersection becomes empty. The returned core index is checked by the naive subset criterion on sampled queries. No germ identities, label associations, zero semantics, or signed branch assignments are deleted. This is only an index of previously verified failures, not a replacement for the full suffix predicate; empty J(A) is UNKNOWN. Storage is 98*m incidence bits plus core originals and intersection work proportional to the number of absent germs times ceil(m/wordsize). No overall runtime improvement claimed without timing comparison.

Use all previous full depth-5 failed branches from R304 and the R303 antichain, not new greedy shrinking. The index is frozen during this sweep; new full failures are retained for a later extension. The original exact recursion still performs the necessary test on index misses. Negative memo insertions by depth are measured without additional solving. A prospective proof-DAG core extraction can use a failed child witness for each split and their union, plus one germ for every label when the parent is saturated; this keeps the same necessary-wall library for the smaller parent. This is not an executed minimizer.

The initial direct-main publication received a definite 409 expected-head conflict caused by a concurrent unrelated T6 commit. The target file was confirmed absent; the deterministic calculation was replayed for preservation and its key counts and frontier matched. No duplicate scientific progress is counted.
